# Cold Start Problem — Network Effects Playbook Skill for Muse

Distills Andrew Chen's *The Cold Start Problem* into an actionable launch-and-growth playbook for networked products — marketplaces, social apps, messaging, collaboration tools: it scores your launch plan 0-10, then walks you through the five stages (cold start, tipping point, escape velocity, hitting the ceiling, the moat), with atomic-network scoping, the hard-side-first principle (solve for sellers/creators/organizers before the easy side), tipping playbooks (invite-only, paid launch, seeding), and an eight-mistake diagnostic with fixes. Discovered via skills.sh. Honest note: this is a strategy framework drawn from a book, not a plug-and-play growth tool — it gives you sharp questions and scored answers, not users; examples and case-study references live in the repo's references/ folder, fetch them too. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use. Not verified.
